_note: Single source of truth. INDEX.md and docs/families/*.md are generated from this file by generate_docs.py and must never be hand-edited. Only shipped models appear here: a registry entry for a script that does not exist would route an agent to a dead path.

families.question: Can this design answer my question at all, and how much data do I need?
How big is it, and how sure am I?

models.title: Minimum attainable p-value for this design
situations: can this test even reach significance with so few runs
is my sample too small to prove anything
three runs each, can I get a p value
why can't I get a significant result from this comparison
before and after on five items, is that enough
models.output: smallest p the design can produce, and whether alpha is reachable at all
models.refuses_when: a group size below 1, both designs given at once, or alpha outside (0,1)
models.evidence: No recorded baseline in evals/baselines/ mentioned the attainability floor. Encodes a fact rather than a computation.

models.title: Benchmark runs needed per arm
situations: how many times should I run this benchmark
how many samples do I need to detect a slowdown
is five runs enough to tell if it got slower
how much data do I need before I can decide
planning a performance comparison, what sample size
models.output: runs per arm needed; with --pilot, widened for uncertainty in the sd estimate
models.baseline_to_beat: the conventional default of 30 runs per arm
models.refuses_when: effect not positive, neither or both of --sd/--pilot, fewer than 2 pilot values, or zero pilot spread
models.unanswerable_when: the required runs exceed what any workflow could execute, meaning the effect is not measurable against this noise
composition_hazards: Do not feed the same pilot runs into the comparison you are sizing. Reusing them makes the test optimistic; collect fresh runs.
models.data_provenance_required: pilot runs must be interleaved or randomised, not all-old-then-all-new; sequential collection makes the sd estimate reflect drift rather than noise
models.evidence: Baseline S1 computed a correct Welch t-test on 5 runs and never asked how many were needed; it scored 3/4 for that omission.

models.title: Three-point estimate to a range (beta-PERT)
situations: how long will this take, best case worst case most likely
turn optimistic and pessimistic estimates into a date
what date should I commit to and with what confidence
give me a range from a three point estimate
PERT estimate for this project
models.output: mean, correct sd, requested percentiles, and the error in the textbook sd
models.refuses_when: estimates not ordered optimistic <= likely <= pessimistic, or zero range
composition_hazards: Summing per-task PERT estimates understates the total's spread unless the tasks are independent, and understates the duration of parallel workstreams entirely, where the finish time is the maximum rather than the sum.
models.evidence: Baseline S5 used the textbook sd (b-a)/6, which is not the standard deviation of the distribution whose mean is (a+4m+b)/6. Corrects a formula reproduced wrongly.

models.title: Unmeasured-confounding breakdown value (E-value)
situations: how fragile is this causal claim to something we didn't measure
could a confounder explain away this association
we controlled for the obvious things, is that enough
how strong would a hidden variable have to be to kill this result
is this correlation actually causal
models.usage: (--rr X | --or X [--rare] | --hr X | --smd D) [--ci-low L --ci-high H]
models.output: the confounder-association strength needed with both exposure and outcome to nullify the effect
models.refuses_when: a non-positive ratio, --rare without --or, one confidence limit without the other, or a reversed interval
models.unanswerable_when: the observed effect sits exactly on the null, so there is no association to explain away
composition_hazards: The E-value bounds unmeasured confounding only. It says nothing about selection bias, measurement error, or reverse causation, and quoting it as general robustness overstates what it covers.
models.data_provenance_required: the effect must already be adjusted for measured confounders; an unadjusted estimate makes the E-value meaningless
models.evidence: Reports a breakdown value rather than an assumption test, per principle P4: screening on a low-power assumption check selects for datasets where the violation was invisible.
